title: Main Deck Cargo Floor Panels Frames 40 to 54 — Removal
abstract: Removal of the main deck cargo floor panels between frames 40 and 54, with the panel support sequence that stops a panel tipping into the bay when its end fasteners come out.

sections.purpose: This task removes the cargo floor panels between frames 40 and 54 so that the floor beam structure, the gusset kits and the splice plates below them become accessible.
sections.job_setup_note: Do this task with the aircraft on the ground and the cabin floor covering and seats already removed over the working area. The panels are large and will tip if they are unsupported when the end fasteners come out; the support frame is not optional. Work bay by bay and do not open more than two adjacent bays at once, so that the floor stays walkable.
sections.procedure: 1. Remove the cabin floor covering and the seats over the working area, zone 225. 2. Get access to the cargo compartment below through access panels 133BR and 142CL to confirm that nothing is stowed under the panels. 3. Mark each panel with its bay number and orientation before anything is loosened. 4. Fit the panel support frame under the first panel. CAUTION: THE PANELS ARE HEAVY AND WILL TIP WHEN THE END FASTENERS ARE REMOVED. FIT THE SUPPORT FRAME FIRST. 5. Remove the countersunk screws AGS895094-3D from the panel edges, working from the centre outwards. 6. Lower the panel onto the support frame and move it clear. 7. Repeat for the second panel of the bay. 8. Do a visual check of the aft cargo floor gusset kit D5350137657469 and the forward splice plate sub-assembly ES657922-93 in the open bay. 9. Cover the open bay with the temporary walkway before any person crosses it. WARNING: DO NOT WALK ON AN OPEN BAY WITHOUT THE TEMPORARY WALKWAY IN POSITION. 10. Move to the next bay and repeat.
sections.close_out: Stack the removed panels in bay order on the protective mat. Make sure that the seat track lock actuator position 8300VU is not disturbed. Record which bays are open and confirm the temporary walkway is in place before the shift changes.

safety_precautions: Fit the panel support frame before the end fasteners are removed.
Do not walk on an open bay without the temporary walkway.
Make sure nothing is stowed in the compartment below.

title: Main Deck Cargo Floor Panels Frames 40 to 54 — Removal

issue.reason: The hard point positions, their protective caps and the panel removal order around them are added, and the bay is no longer opened from the centre outwards where hard points are fitted.

abstract: Removal of the main deck cargo floor panels between frames 40 and 54, with the panel support sequence that stops a panel tipping into the bay and the handling the freighter hard points need where they are fitted.

sections.purpose: This task removes the cargo floor panels between frames 40 and 54 so that the floor beam structure, the gusset kits and the splice plates below them become accessible.
sections.job_setup_note: Do this task with the aircraft on the ground and the cabin floor covering and seats already removed over the working area. The panels are large and will tip if they are unsupported when the end fasteners come out; the support frame is not optional. Work bay by bay and do not open more than two adjacent bays at once, so that the floor stays walkable. On a provisioned aircraft there are four hard points in each bay, one at each corner of the panel pair, and they change how the bay is opened: the panel edge over a hard point is stiffer than the rest, so a panel released from the centre outwards will hinge on the hard point line and load the two corner screws. Release those four positions first. The hard points are capped in passenger configuration and the cap is a structural item, not a dust cover; a cap left off admits water into the lug bore and the lug is not inspectable with the panel on.
sections.procedure: 1. Remove the cabin floor covering and the seats over the working area, zone 225. 2. Get access to the cargo compartment below through access panels 133BR and 142CL to confirm that nothing is stowed under the panels. 3. Mark each panel with its bay number and orientation before anything is loosened. 4. Establish from the aircraft configuration whether the bay is provisioned with hard points. 5. Fit the panel support frame under the first panel. CAUTION: THE PANELS ARE HEAVY AND WILL TIP WHEN THE END FASTENERS ARE REMOVED. FIT THE SUPPORT FRAME FIRST. 6. On a provisioned bay, release the four screws over the hard point positions first, then work from the centre outwards. On an unprovisioned bay, work from the centre outwards throughout. 7. Remove the countersunk screws AGS895094-3D from the panel edges. 8. Lower the panel onto the support frame and move it clear. 9. Repeat for the second panel of the bay. 10. Do a visual check of the aft cargo floor gusset kit D5350137657469 and the forward splice plate sub-assembly ES657922-93 in the open bay. 11. Where the freighter hard points are fitted, remove each cap from the upper lug sub-assembly HA342629-96, check the lug bore for corrosion and standing water, re-grease the bore and refit the cap with a new seal. CAUTION: DO NOT LEAVE A HARD POINT UNCAPPED WITH THE PANEL OFF. SWARF AND SEALANT FROM THE SURROUNDING WORK WILL ENTER THE BORE AND THE LUG CANNOT BE CLEANED WITH THE PANEL BACK ON. 12. Cover the open bay with the temporary walkway before any person crosses it. WARNING: DO NOT WALK ON AN OPEN BAY WITHOUT THE TEMPORARY WALKWAY IN POSITION. 13. Move to the next bay and repeat.
sections.close_out: Stack the removed panels in bay order on the protective mat. Make sure that the seat track lock actuator position 8300VU is not disturbed. On a provisioned aircraft, confirm that every hard point cap is refitted and record the lug bore condition against the bay number. Record which bays are open and confirm the temporary walkway is in place before the shift changes.

type_data.effectivity_note: All SOLANO-30 and SOLANO-34 aircraft; steps 4, 6 and 11 apply only to aircraft post MOD-132210

safety_precautions: Fit the panel support frame before the end fasteners are removed.
Do not walk on an open bay without the temporary walkway.
Refit every hard point cap before the bay is left.
